What did the DLP scanner actually read?

A text prompt and a PNG both produced zero findings. Four local runs of AI DLP Guard show how to tell which content was inspected.

Martin Stefanov

A request for a meeting agenda and an image of the words “Workshop agenda” can both produce zero findings in a data loss prevention scan. For an analyst deciding whether the content can go to an AI service, those two results carry very different information.

Start with a readable control

In a local run of the AI DLP Guard 2.1.0 workstation agent, “Draft a short meeting agenda.” returned full inspection coverage and an allow decision. A second prompt, “Please remind demo@example.com about the workshop.”, produced one email finding. Running the redaction option on that text returned “Please remind [ИМЕЙЛ-1] about the workshop.” The recipient was masked, and the task itself was still intelligible.

Give the agent an image

The same CLI was given a PNG containing only the words “Workshop agenda”. The workstation package has no image OCR. The scan reported that it had inspected none of the image content. With the other file settings left at their defaults, changing the failure mode changed the outcome.

Input Coverage Findings Decision Exit
Plain agenda request Full 0 Allow 0
Reminder with an address Full 1 email Sanitize 1
Agenda PNG, open mode None 0 Warn 0
Same PNG, closed mode None 0 Block 1

A CI job that keeps only the process exit status loses the distinction between the first and third rows. It also groups a successful redaction with a block in the other two. The structured output from scan --json preserves the coverage, detector counts and decision separately. The browser extension includes its own OCR, so its result for an image needs a separate test.

Preserve the distinction in reports

For an unreadable file, the most useful next question is which input type and channel produced it. If all such events came from the workstation agent and involved images, there is a specific capability to evaluate. Combined with the active policy version, those fields can explain a change in warning volume without copying the original prompt into the event.
